title: Mutations in glioblastoma proteins do not disrupt epitope presentation and recognition, maintaining a specific CD8 T cell immune response potential.
authors: Tarabini, Renata Fioravanti; Fioravanti Vieira, Gustavo; Rigo, Mauricio Menegatti; de Souza, Ana Paula Duarte
one_liner_zh: 该文研究胶质母细胞瘤蛋白突变对pMHC-I表位呈递与CD8 T细胞识别的影响，涉及蛋白-肽-MHC复合物建模与MD模拟，但核心是免疫表位而非TF-DNA互作，方法可迁移但对象偏离。
abstract: Antigen-specific cytotoxic CD8 T cells are extremely effective in controlling tumor growth and have been the focus of immunotherapy approaches. We leverage in silico tools to investigate whether the occurrence of mutations in proteins previously described as immunogenic and highly expressed by glioblastoma multiforme (GBM), such as Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR), Isocitrate Dehydrogenase 1 (IDH1), Phosphatase and Tensin homolog (PTEN) and Tumor Protein 53 (TP53), may be contributing to the differential presentation of immunogenic epitopes. We recovered Class I MHC binding information from wild-type and mutated proteins using the Immune Epitope Database (IEDB). After that, we built peptide-MHC (pMHC-I) models in HLA-arena, followed by hierarchical clustering analysis based on electrostatic surface features from each complex. We identified point mutations that are determinants for the presentation of a set of peptides from TP53 protein. We point to structural features in the pMHC-I complexes of wild-type and mutated peptides, which may play a role in the recognition of CD8 T cells. To further explore these features, we performed 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations for the peptide pairs (wt/mut) selected. In pursuit of novel therapeutic targets for GBM treatment, we selected peptides where our predictive results indicated that mutations would not disrupt epitope presentation, thereby maintaining a specific CD8 T cell immune response. These peptides hold potential for future GBM interventions, including peptide-based or mRNA vaccine development applications.
abstract_zh: 抗原特异性细胞毒性CD8 T细胞在控制肿瘤生长方面极为有效，并已成为免疫治疗方法的焦点。我们利用计算机模拟工具（in silico tools）研究先前被描述为具有免疫原性且在胶质母细胞瘤（glioblastoma multiforme, GBM）中高表达的蛋白质（如表皮生长因子受体（Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor, EGFR）、异柠檬酸脱氢酶1（Isocitrate Dehydrogenase 1, IDH1）、磷酸酶与张力蛋白同源物（Phosphatase and Tensin homolog, PTEN）和肿瘤蛋白53（Tumor Protein 53, TP53））中发生的突变是否可能促进免疫原性表位的差异性呈递。我们使用免疫表位数据库（Immune Epitope Database, IEDB）回收了野生型和突变型蛋白的I类MHC结合信息。之后，我们在HLA-arena中构建了肽-MHC（pMHC-I）模型，并基于每个复合物的静电表面特征进行层次聚类分析。我们识别出决定TP53蛋白一组肽段呈递的点突变。我们指出了野生型和突变型肽段的pMHC-I复合物中的结构特征，这些特征可能在CD8 T细胞识别中发挥作用。为进一步探索这些特征，我们对选定的肽对（wt/mut）进行了100 ns的分子动力学（molecular dynamics）模拟。为寻求GBM治疗的新治疗靶点，我们选择了预测结果表明突变不会破坏表位呈递的肽段，从而维持特异性CD8 T细胞免疫应答。这些肽段具有未来GBM干预的潜力，包括基于肽段或mRNA疫苗的开发应用。
